study.question: At fixed forward-normalized aligned target/history products, does removing inverse-norm gradient scaling retain or improve validation performance, and does its effect depend on radial projection? Observed: full aligned normalization AUC=0.6149816911798147, Logloss=0.19656340759133067 versus detached aligned AUC=0.6145833321081287, Logloss=0.19663658831646288: full-minus-detached +0.0003983590716861 AUC and -0.0000731807251322 Logloss. Both existing arms still scale by 1/r, so its contribution and interaction with projection are unresolved. Crossed full-minus-detached AUC is only +0.0000460763438621 and Logloss worsens +0.0001258864593347; this does not justify a universal normalization story. The requested paired-seed replication is scientifically preferable for robustness but the current interface fixes train_seed=42 and exposes no seed operation. This bounded two-job attribution study answers a different, source-auditable uncertainty while retaining replication resources.
study.hypothesis: Above the norm floor, full normalization composes radial projection P=I-u*u^T with inverse-norm scaling 1/r. The observed aligned full-versus-detached advantage may reflect useful suppression of product-magnitude gradients, while 1/r need not be essential and may attenuate the product pathway relative to unchanged shared-embedding pathways. Prediction: tangent-only backward P, with the same forward u, beats identity backward I and can retain or improve the full incumbent. This is a provisional optimization-pathway hypothesis, not semantic relevance, probability calibration, statistical significance or literature novelty. At the floor all four modes use I/1e-3; the factors are defined only above the floor. No floor event occurred in the supplied first-512 aligned/crossed diagnostics, which does not establish the full training population floor rate.

The proposed change is only the aligned normalized product backward path.

study.proposed_difference: Two standalone modules add normalization_gradient=tangent and identity; pairing stays aligned and forward normalization stays unit. Let stop(x) detach its argument. Tangent uses surrogate s=u*stop(where(sum(p*p)>=1e-6,r,1)); identity uses s=p*stop(where(sum(p*p)>=1e-6,1,1/r)). Both return stop(u)+(s-stop(s)), so finite same-state forward arithmetic is unchanged while Jacobians become P and I above the floor. Parentheses ensure an exactly zero finite forward correction rather than an avoidable subtraction-rounding drift. At equality the regular branch follows the inherited clamp active-side convention; numerical finite-difference checks avoid this nondifferentiable boundary. Reuse r0005-normalized_aligned as A=1,B=1 (full J=(I-u*u^T)/r; candidate.py SHA256 a93bfe8357fbbf08f0250d169cb41eb02f637a3f5a4dc1d7b8a4c4a84e293aa3); reuse r0006-aligned_detached as A=0,B=1 (J=I/r; history_r0006_aligned_detached.py SHA256 f724f68f917b6befd2c5151f0c70bf2212aab36e324c459f664d26ee532aebeb). A denotes radial projection and B inverse-norm scaling, for nonfloored events. New tangent is A=1,B=0; new identity is A=0,B=0. Use only compatible seed-42 receipts; do not silently change seeds to satisfy the earlier replication request. No new training results are claimed. Local checks: both modules compile in memory, only numeric torch imports, constructor and all unaffected methods match incumbent AST, class bodies match each other, and diagnostics statically total 62 finite-scalar candidates (host must confirm finiteness). Torch is absent, so no tensor execution or autograd verification occurred. Independent ordinary-Python scalar finite differences checked all four declared surrogate Jacobians on zero, floored, nonfloored, near-floor and large vectors (20 cases; maximum scaled error 8.23e-11). This verifies the formulas rather than actual PyTorch backward execution. Host diagnostics retain inherited label-free first-512 measurements and add mode flags, full-versus-surrogate same-state product/logit differences, inverse-norm mean and floor counts. They run under no_grad and cannot verify gradients or establish representative relevance.

falsifiers: Tangent-minus-identity AUC<=0 weakens the radial-projection explanation without inverse-norm scaling; disagreement with full-minus-detached indicates scaling dependence or interaction rather than a general projection benefit.

Tangent-minus-full AUC<0 rejects the specific expectation that projection alone retains/improves incumbent ranking performance at this seed. If Logloss improves while AUC falls, retain the tradeoff rather than declare success under the primary metric.

If the two new cells both underperform the incumbent or the inverse-scaling effects favor 1/r at both projection settings, keep the incumbent and close this bounded no-scaling direction; do not launch a strength sweep automatically.

Nonfinite logits/gradients, mismatched sources/configs/constructor, forward mismatch, unexpected parameter differences or changed recipe invalidate attribution and require a recorded implementation failure, not reinterpretation as a mechanism null.
